standards.name: FAIR Genomes metadata schema
standards.abstract: The FAIR Genomes schema describes metadata for human genomic (NGS) data generated in clinical and research settings in the Netherlands. It covers people/participants, consent (leaflet and individual consent), clinical information, materials and samples, sample preparation, sequencing and analysis results; metadata is represented in a semantic/YAML model and can be transformed into JSON, RDF and data-entry templates. The standard was developed by the FAIR Genomes consortium (14+ Dutch medical centers and collaborators) to increase FAIRness (Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, Reusability) of NGS data, harmonize element definitions using existing ontologies (NCIT, DUO, EDAM, HPO etc.), and to support ELSI/consent encoding and practical implementations (MOLGENIS, codebooks). The published schema v1.1 contains 110 elements grouped into 9 modules and is distributed with documentation, codebooks and a MOLGENIS reference implementation.

classification.rationale: The source material is a semantic metadata schema presented as concrete modules and elements with explicit element names, descriptions and preferred data/value types (e.g. string, date, integer, lookups/ontologies). The Supplementary Data and codebook/TSV files provide field-level structure (columns: element name, description, value type, references), which matches the definition of a TABLE in the extraction guidelines.

standards.notes: The FAIR Genomes schema v1.1 is a comprehensive semantic model (110 elements in 9 modules) and the complete specification, lookups and codebooks are available in the Supplementary Data and the project's GitHub (e.g. Supplementary Data S2, fairgenomes_molgenis_app data TSVs, and https://fairgenomes.org). I extracted representative fields from multiple source files (Supplementary Data S2 and published TSV/codebook files) with verbatim evidence quotes. For the full set of elements and lookups (including 85307 lookups mentioned in Supplementary Data S2), consult the original schema distribution.
